A.summary: It is the severity of the harm described in the VIS, not the presence of the VIS itself, that leads to heavier sentences.

B.summary: Sentencing is influenced by both the harm described and the strong emotions expressed in the VIS, so the VIS itself induces a heavier sentence.

c1.text: Sentences tend to be heavier when a VIS is submitted compared to when it is not.

c2.text: It is the severity of the harm described in the VIS, not the presence of the VIS itself, that leads to heavier sentences.

c3.text: Victims who have suffered more serious harm are more likely to submit a VIS, whereas victims who have not suffered serious harm tend not to submit a VIS.

c4.text: Judges and jurors are influenced by both the harm described in the VIS and the strong emotions expressed by the victim through the VIS.

c5.text: The VIS itself induces a heavier sentence.

c6.text: In Method P, Group 1 receives a VIS describing emotional injury much more serious than generally expected, Group 2 receives a VIS describing emotional injury less serious than generally expected, and Group 3 receives no VIS.

c7.text: In Method Q, Group 1 sees a video of a serious VIS read in a highly emotional manner, Group 2 sees the same VIS read calmly, and Group 3 sees a less serious VIS read calmly.

c8.text: In Method P, the severity of harm mock jurors are exposed to is in the order of Group 1, Group 3, and Group 2.

c9.text: In Method Q, Group 1 and Group 2 differ only in emotional expression, while Group 2 and Group 3 differ only in the severity of harm described.

ha1.text: In Method P, the average sentence of Group 1 is significantly higher than that of Group 2, and the average sentence of Group 2 is significantly higher than that of Group 3.

ha2.text: The presence of the VIS itself leads to a heavier sentence regardless of the severity of the harm.

a.note: In P, harm severity is Group 1 > Group 3 > Group 2. Group 2 > Group 3 shows the VIS itself increases sentencing despite less severe harm, which contradicts View A.

hb1.text: In Method Q, the average sentence of Group 1 is significantly higher than that of Group 2, and the average sentence of Group 2 is significantly higher than that of Group 3.

hb2.text: Both the emotional expression of the victim and the severity of the harm described in the VIS influence sentencing.

b.note: Group 1 > Group 2 shows emotional expression affects sentencing, and Group 2 > Group 3 shows harm severity affects sentencing, together strengthening View B.

hc1.text: In Method Q, comparing only Group 1 and Group 2, there is no significant difference in the average sentence between the two groups.

hc2.text: Sentencing is not influenced by emotional expression in the VIS, but depends on the severity of the harm described.

c.note: No difference between Group 1 and Group 2 shows emotional delivery does not affect sentencing when harm is identical, which supports View A rather than weakening it.
